title: Modeling the Dynamics of the Marburg Virus Disease
abstract: This work models the infection dynamics of the Marburg Virus Disease using the SEIQR model. It is a five-compartment model. We investigated the non-negativity of solutions, invariant region and boundedness, equilibrium points, basic reproduction number, sensitivity, equilibrium points’ stability, and bifurcation of the model. For all time and positive initial conditions, we observed that the model has non-negative solutions. The invariant region of the model is established, revealing the population size is bounded. The sensitivity analysis shows that the contact rate, the probability of effective contact and the rate at which exposed individuals become infectious have positive sensitivity indices, while the quarantine rates for the exposed and infectious classes, the death rates, and the recovery rates for the exposed and infectious classes have negative sensitivity indices. We established that the non-negativity of the residual vector , resulting from the difference between the rate of change of infected individuals and the Metzler matrix, stops the existence of several endemic equilibria for . Thus, no critical value exists, and there is an extension of local stability of the disease-free equilibrium to global stability on the entire domain. The bifurcation analysis reveals a forward bifurcation and the bifurcation plot confirms that for effective management and eradication the disease, the basic reproduction number must satisfy , where is a critical value. The mathematical analysis also reveals that the disease-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable. The effects of some sensitive parameters on the infectious class are shown via numerical simulations.

title: Pseudovirus Nanoparticles Displaying the Receptor-Binding Glycoprotein of Marburg Virus as Potential Vaccine Candidates
abstract: Background: The lack of a licensed vaccine against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) calls for the development of a novel and effective vaccine strategy. Methods: We report here our development of three pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs), each displaying a MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP) segment of different lengths, as MARV vaccine candidates. These PVNPs, designated S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, were generated using our proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform. The PVNPs were evaluated for their production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results: Our data demonstrated that the three recombinant S-GP proteins, S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, can be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system. The purified recombinant S-GP proteins self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling of the S-GP1 PVNPs highlighted their key architectural features, consisting of an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures displayed on the surface. Immunization of mice with the S-GP PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. Conclusions: Collectively, these data support the notion that the S-GP PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates worthy of further development.

abstract_zh: 背景:缺乏针对致命 马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 的许可 疫苗 需要开发一种新颖且有效的 疫苗 策略。方法:我们在这里报告了我们开发的三种假病毒纳米粒子(PVNP),每个纳米粒子都显示不同长度的 MARV 中和糖蛋白(GP)片段,作为 MARV 疫苗 候选者。这些 PVNP 被命名为 S-GP278、S-GP377 和 S-GP486,是使用我们专有的诺如病毒壳纳米颗粒 (SNP) 平台生成的。对 PVNP 的生产、自组装、形态、结构特性和免疫原性进行了评估。结果:我们的数据表明,可以使用大肠杆菌表达系统以低成本生产三种重组 S-GP 蛋白 S-GP278、S-GP377 和 S-GP486。纯化的重组S-GP蛋白高效自组装成PVNP。S-GP1 PVNP 的结构建模突出了它们的关键结构特征,包括二十面体内壳和表面显示的多个三聚体 GP 结构。用 S-GP PVNP 免疫小鼠可引发高滴度的 GP 特异性抗体,包括 IgG 和 IgA。结论:总的来说,这些数据支持这样的观点,即 S-GP PVNP 可以作为值得进一步开发的潜在 MARV 疫苗 候选药物。

title: Bat-borne zoonoses: transmission, impact, prevention, and management.
abstract: Abstract Climate change and biodiversity loss are global environmental crises driving emerging infectious diseases, including bat-borne pathogens of public health significance: Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, classic rabies virus, and Australian bat lyssavirus, as well as the fungus Histoplasma . This review presents the evidence on the mechanisms of transmission, impact, and prevention and management strategies relevant to each of these pathogens. Transmission pathways vary between pathogens but often involve exposure to body fluids or excreta of a bat or other infected animal or human. The diseases associated with these infections have high mortality rates, and survivors may continue to experience a range of long term effects, including neurological and neuropsychiatric signs and symptoms. Prevention strategies may be implemented to reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover and human-to-human transmission of these pathogens, including better ecological stewardship, reducing exposure of domestic animals and humans to bats, isolation of infected people, and, where possible, vaccination of humans and animals. The mainstay of treatment for these conditions is supportive care; however, specific drugs are now available for histoplasmosis and Ebolavirus infection. In the face of climate change and further loss of biodiversity, developing more effective strategies to prevent and manage these conditions will be critical.

title: Cross-border preparedness, health worker protection, and institutional response in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
abstract: This Perspective presents the author’s own analytical position on the international response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, rather than a systematic assessment of the evidence. On 17 May 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), the second-highest alert level under the International Health Regulations (IHR) as amended in 2024. Three interlinked themes are examined: cross-border preparedness under the amended IHR and the WHO Pandemic Agreement (adopted 2025, not yet in force); frontline health worker protection, illustrated by four healthcare-worker deaths within four days of the initial alert; and institutional response and research investment, illustrated by the continued absence of a licensed, Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic and by disparities in access to advanced care. Genuine early action has coexisted with weak cross-border screening coordination, gaps in healthcare worker protection, and limited community engagement, illustrated by the burning of an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara; these gaps appear, on the evidence available, to reflect governance weaknesses, financing shortfalls, and insecurity rather than any single cause. The Perspective closes with recommendations on cross-border surveillance protocols, healthcare worker protection, community engagement, and equitable neglected-pathogen research investment, for policymakers, Africa CDC, WHO, and practitioners.

title: Community barriers, perceptions, and health-seeking behaviors within the one health approach in six priority districts of Rwanda: a descriptive qualitative study
abstract: Rwanda’s health security can only be strengthened through integrated One Health approaches that link human, animal, and environmental health. Emerging health threats such as the Marburg Virus highlight the urgency, yet fragmented systems, weak coordination, and behavioral barriers continue to constrain resilience. Thus, we assessed behavioral, social, and systemic determinants influencing community resilience, outbreak preparedness, and response, using the Health Belief Model (HBM) and the Social Ecological Model (SEM) to generate actionable evidence for strengthening One Health integration, health system performance, and risk communication strategies for effective disease prevention and outbreak mitigation in Rwanda. Our descriptive qualitative assessment included participants from Rulindo, Kayonza, Nyanza, Rusizi, Rubavu, and Nyaruguru districts of Rwanda. We had six In-depth Interviews (IDIs) per district and two Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) per district. Participants were selected from different socioeconomic class, occupation selected rotated across districts, ensuring inclusivity, while data collection was carried out in October 2025. We conducted weekly debriefing meetings, which enabled us to familiarize ourselves with the data. Using Dedoose for data coding, results were presented according to themes, while indicating areas of convergence. We received ethical approval for this study from the Rwanda National Ethics Committee (IRB00001497 of IORG0001100). A total of 143 participants took part in the FGDs; the majority were male ( n = 82, 57.34%) and were aged between 31 and 40. Most participants were working as the animal health personnel, n = 19 (13.29%). Of the 36 participants in the IDIs, almost half ( n = 15, 41.7%) were aged 31–40 years. The most commonly reported occupation was being health personnel, n = 12 (33.32%). Several themes emerged; however, using the joint display method of comparing findings from IDIs and FGDs, we identified data convergent points to include factors influencing healthcare-seeking behavior, economic constraints and the deprioritization of health interventions, perceived importance of One Health and weak intersectoral collaboration, community health information dissemination through multiple communication channels and myths and misinformation leads to vaccine rejection, as well as maintaining proper handwashing is a challenge. Findings from this assessment provide a critical foundation for identifying behavioral and systemic gaps and facilitators towards the One Health approach. Bottleneck challenges on resources and limited engagement of community members continue to promote health insecurity. Therefore, district-level coordination and accountability, as well as training of community health workers to listen and engage community members, will enhance the One Health sector of Rwanda.

title_zh: 卢旺达六个优先地区单一健康方法中的社区障碍、观念和寻求健康的行为:一项描述性定性研究
source_body_en: Rwanda’s health security can only be strengthened through integrated One Health approaches that link human, animal, and environmental health. Emerging health threats such as the Marburg Virus highlight the urgency, yet fragmented systems, weak coordination, and behavioral barriers continue to constrain resilience. Thus, we assessed behavioral, social, and systemic determinants influencing community resilience, outbreak preparedness, and response, using the Health Belief Model (HBM) and the Social Ecological Model (SEM) to generate actionable evidence for strengthening One Health integration, health system performance, and risk communication strategies for effective disease prevention and outbreak mitigation in Rwanda. Our descriptive qualitative assessment included participants from Rulindo, Kayonza, Nyanza, Rusizi, Rubavu, and Nyaruguru districts of Rwanda. We had six In-depth Interviews (IDIs) per district and two Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) per district. Participants were selected from different socioeconomic class, occupation selected rotated across districts, ensuring inclusivity, while data collection was carried out in October 2025. We conducted weekly debriefing meetings, which enabled us to familiarize ourselves with the data. Using Dedoose for data coding, results were presented according to themes, while indicating areas of convergence. We received ethical approval for this study from the Rwanda National Ethics Committee (IRB00001497 of IORG0001100). A total of 143 participants took part in the FGDs; the majority were male ( n = 82, 57.34%) and were aged between 31 and 40. Most participants were working as the animal health personnel, n = 19 (13.29%). Of the 36 participants in the IDIs, almost half ( n = 15, 41.7%) were aged 31–40 years. The most commonly reported occupation was being health personnel, n = 12 (33.32%). Several themes emerged; however, using the joint display method of comparing findings from IDIs and FGDs, we identified data convergent points to include factors influencing healthcare-seeking behavior, economic constraints and the deprioritization of health interventions, perceived importance of One Health and weak intersectoral collaboration, community health information dissemination through multiple communication channels and myths and misinformation leads to vaccine rejection, as well as maintaining proper handwashing is a challenge. Findings from this assessment provide a critical foundation for identifying behavioral and systemic gaps and facilitators towards the One Health approach. Bottleneck challenges on resources and limited engagement of community members continue to promote health insecurity. Therefore, district-level coordination and accountability, as well as training of community health workers to listen and engage community members, will enhance the One Health sector of Rwanda.

title: Bundibugyo virus carries a genus-exclusive four-position VP24 configuration and a predicted cell-type ordering of interferon restriction
abstract: Abstract Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) has caused outbreaks with lower case-fatality than Ebola virus (EBOV), and its VP24 carries the one BDBV-specific functional difference mapped to date. That mapping used an engineered virus, so whether BDBV itself carries the configuration, and what the defect implies beyond one cell line, were unknown. We combined a sequence census of deposited BDBV VP24 records, a cell-type-resolved human expression atlas and a reanalysis of public infection data. Every full-length BDBV VP24 record and every complete 2026 outbreak genome carried the four-position configuration (S83/Q135/H140/A141), and no other orthoebolavirus did; a wider re-read found two unconfirmed single-position departures among 860 callable copies. Across 154 human cell types, baseline interferon (IFN)-system expression defined a cell-type-resolved score, Δ, read as the IFN-stimulated level a cell attains, and a competing importin-α account (the rival). In the one panel carrying a functional phenotype, only that post-IFN level held under every probe-aggregation rule (AUC, area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve: 0.83 to 0.90, against 0.67 to 0.80 for the seventeen-gene module's baseline and 0.50 to 0.77 for fold induction). Applied to the defect, that score places urothelium, the airway ciliated cell and circulating myeloid cells highest and the retinal and testicular compartments lowest. We state that ordering as an ordering hypothesis: it converts the cost of a fixed viral defect into a cell-type-resolved, falsifiable prediction, and the framework states the test that would refute it.

title: Case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo with Lack of Transmission to Breastfeeding Infant
abstract: Disease due to Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an Orthoebolavirus species, reemerged in April 2026, in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. A 35-year-old woman transported the body of a possible BDBV-infected patient from Bunia in Ituri Province to Goma for burial; she was accompanied by an 8-month-old breastfeeding child. Six days after arrival in Goma, she noted onset of fever and malaise and was empirically started on therapy for malaria; 4 days later she developed bloody diarrhea and a bloody vaginal discharge and was started on metronidazole for possible amebic dysentery. When her condition worsened she was admitted to hospital in Goma, where a blood sample was positive by real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test for BDBV, with a second positive test on hospital day 7. By day 14 of hospitalization fever and major symptoms had resolved and repeat RT-PCR tests × 2 were negative. Her child did not show evidence of infection, and no family members or health care workers at HEAL Africa Hospital developed illness.

full_text: Abstract Marburg virus (MARV) is an extremely virulent pathogen for which effective preventive and therapeutic strategis remain limited, highlighting the urgent demand for a safe and efficient vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-based approach was employed to design a novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine capable of eliciting robust humoral and cell mediated immune responses. Highly conserved cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were systematically predicted and assembled using GGGS, GPGPG and KK linkers respectively. To enhance immunogenicity, the construct was fused with the 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant, while a PADRE sequence was incorporated to promote broad CD4+ T-cell activation across diverse HLA alleles. The three-dimensional structure of the vaccine construct was modelled, refined and evaluated for stability and structural integrity using validation tools including ERRAT, Ramachandran plot analysis, MolProbity scoring, and RMSD assessment. Molecular docking studies revealed strong and stable interactions between the vaccine and immune receptors, as reflected by a favourable HDOCK score (− 315.21) and a high confidence value (0.9646). Additionally, normal mode analysis conducted via iMODS demonstrated appropriate molecular flexibility, indicated by a low eigen value (3.61×10–6), supporting effective receptor engagement and immune activation. Immune simulations revealed strong humoral and cellular immune responses, marked by increased levels of IgG and IgM, cytokine secretion (IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF-α), and the development of memory cells. The optimized gene attained a Codon Adaptation Index (CAI) of 1.0 along with a GC content of 54.49%, indicating its appropriateness for expression in Escherichia coli utilizing the pET-28a( +) vector. In summary, the Insilico results present the constructed vaccine as a promising multi-epitope candidate against the Marburg virus, necessitating additional experimental tests to validate its immunogenic effectiveness and protective capability. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Marburg virus (MARV) is an extremely virulent pathogen for which effective preventive and therapeutic strategis remain limited, highlighting the urgent demand for a safe and efficient vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-based approach was employed to design a novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine capable of eliciting robust humoral and cell mediated immune responses. Highly conserved cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were systematically predicted and assembled using GGGS, GPGPG and KK linkers respectively. To enhance immunogenicity, the construct was fused with the 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant, while a PADRE sequence was incorporated to promote broad CD4+ T-cell activation across diverse HLA alleles. The three-dimensional structure of the vaccine construct was modelled, refined and evaluated for stability and structural integrity using validation tools including ERRAT, Ramachandran plot analysis, MolProbity scoring, and RMSD assessment. Molecular docking studies revealed strong and stable interactions between the vaccine and immune receptors, as reflected by a favourable HDOCK score (− 315.21) and a high confidence value (0.9646). Additionally, normal mode analysis conducted via iMODS demonstrated appropriate molecular flexibility, indicated by a low eigen value (3.61×10–6), supporting effective receptor engagement and immune activation. Immune simulations revealed strong humoral and cellular immune responses, marked by increased levels of IgG and IgM, cytokine secretion (IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF-α), and the development of memory cells. The optimized gene attained a Codon Adaptation Index (CAI) of 1.0 along with a GC content of 54.49%, indicating its appropriateness for expression in Escherichia coli utilizing the pET-28a( +) vector. In summary, the Insilico results present the constructed vaccine as a promising multi-epitope candidate against the Marburg virus, necessitating additional experimental tests to validate its immunogenic effectiveness and protective capability. elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算机分析,需要实验验证来确认免疫原性有效性和保护能力。由于依赖于没有经验数据的计算模型,证据强度中等。

title: Adaptation of Bayesian decision analysis for clinical trial design to binary outcomes: illustration for Ebola virus disease treatment
abstract: could benefit seriously ill patients lacking therapeutic alternatives. Bayesian decision analysis (BDA) integrates multiple health consequences into trial design. We extend BDA for trials with binary outcomes to calculate optimal sample sizes (n) and α in an Ebola outbreak context. We consider fixed, two-arm randomized trials with binary outcomes and two types of clinical trial losses: post-trial loss, for not approving an effective treatment or approving an ineffective one; in-trial loss, for not administrating an effective treatment to control-arm patients or for administrating an ineffective treatment to experimental-arm patients. The model incorporates treatment side effects and disease severity into a single loss function, from which BDA-optimal n and α are derived. Using mortality as the outcome, we modeled various epidemic scenarios by varying target population size, mortality rate, and treatment efficacy. In most cases, BDA-optimal α exceeded the conventional one-sided 2.5% and sample sizes are smaller. Simulations comparing BDA-optimized two-arm trials (fixed/sequential) to conventional designs (two-arm/single-arm, fixed/sequential) across outbreak scenarios show comparable statistical power across designs, except when sample size assumptions are incorrect, or when trials started after the outbreak peak; in these situations, BDA-optimized trials show superior powers. This BDA framework provides a promising approach for designing trials with binary outcomes, particularly in high-mortality disease outbreaks, where declining case numbers and uncertain mortality and efficacy data challenge conventional methods.
